Title: May 14, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Study Session
Overview: Council received a financial forecast from CU's Business Research Division and city staff showing flattening sales and property tax revenue, a projected $6.5 million general fund shortfall for 2027, and 4% department reduction targets. Council then reviewed potential 2026 ballot measures and facility funding scenarios and gave staff direction to poll on a parks and public improvement mill levy expansion, up to $200 million in debt (with a split test at $400 million), a charter change to the debt limit, and a general fund debt authorization, while not pursuing a vacancy tax further at this time.

Topic1.Title: Economic conditions and sales tax outlook
Topic1.Summary: CU's Business Research Division reviewed national and Colorado economic conditions, noting slow GDP growth, stalled job growth, and a sharp rise in energy prices and inflation. Retail spending remains nominally positive but declines after adjusting for inflation, and Boulder's sales tax growth trails the state average. Staff's forecast uses the Moody's national outlook and a medium scenario, projecting slow but steady sales and use tax growth.

Topic2.Title: Council questions on economy, recession risk, and water
Topic2.Summary: Council members asked how long energy price effects would last, whether conditions signal recession, and why Colorado is losing jobs. Questions also covered the Federal Reserve, tariffs, and property versus sales tax ratios. A council member noted that water supply was not a variable in the forecast model, and staff said alternative scenarios would address unanticipated shocks.

Topic3.Title: City financial forecast and 2027 budget outlook
Topic3.Summary: Staff reported that the 2026 budget closed a $7.5 million gap through hiring freezes, realignments, and a 7.8% general fund reduction. For 2027, a $6.5 million general fund shortfall led to a request for 4% department reductions. Sales and use tax and property tax revenues are revised down, with the property tax reassessment showing only 0.2% actual value growth.

Topic4.Title: Forecast Q&A, performance-based cuts, and Sundance revenue
Topic4.Summary: Council asked whether programs were cut based on performance measures and how staff would communicate reductions to the public. Members questioned why the medium forecast scenario was chosen and requested more programmatic budget-to-actual detail. Staff said Sundance revenue will be included in the sales tax model as it is received, with a cautious approach in year one.

Topic5.Title: Long-term financial strategy and ballot measure framing
Topic5.Summary: The city manager explained that about 68% of city revenue is committed to specific purposes, so the general fund is constrained. Expense growth has outpaced revenue growth, and a long-term comprehensive financial plan is planned for late 2026. Staff framed the ballot measure work as one component of that strategy.

Topic6.Title: Staff ballot measure options and recommendations
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented four tax ballot options for further exploration: a parks and public improvement mill levy or use expansion, a residential vacancy excise tax, general fund debt authorization, and a public realm sales tax consolidation. Staff recommended polling the parks mill levy and deferring the general fund debt, public realm tax, and vacancy tax to later analysis. Polling is limited to three to four items, with results expected in late June.

Topic7.Title: Facility funding scenarios for priority buildings
Topic7.Summary: Staff reported that 15 priority buildings need roughly $20 million over five to six years for major maintenance, with an estimated $500 million total priority need. Scenarios A through E combined existing CCRS authority with mill levy increases and general obligation bonds. Staff recommended scenarios C and E, which together provide up to $200 million, and a charter change to the 3% debt limit based on actual value.

Topic8.Title: Council direction on polling and ballot items
Topic8.Summary: Council members debated how many items to poll and whether to include the $400 million option, with several supporting a $200 million split test. Many supported polling general fund debt authorization because it could inform future planning, while others raised concerns about taxpayer fatigue. Council also discussed whether the mill levy expansion should include operations, public safety, and the airport.

Topic9.Title: Vacancy excise tax direction
Topic9.Summary: Council members discussed a residential vacancy excise tax on homes vacant at least 183 days, with some proposing a tiered structure based on square footage and a higher maximum. Staff said the legal details would require further research, and council gave consensus to proceed with that analysis. Some members favored an ordinance over a ballot initiative for greater future flexibility, and others raised concerns about unintended consequences.

Topic10.Title: Charter amendments on boards and wildfire mitigation
Topic10.Summary: The charter committee proposed revising charter section 130 on boards and commissions, which failed by 65 votes in 2024, and adding wildfire mitigation as an explicit open space purpose in section 176. Council members debated timing, removal provisions, and whether to add flood mitigation. Staff said wildfire work is already permitted, and council gave direction to continue drafting the wildfire language but not advance the boards and commissions change this year.

Topic11.Title: Community petitions and state and regional ballot measures
Topic11.Summary: Staff noted one community-sponsored petition for a commercial and residential vacancy tax, included in the council packet. Boulder County, the city of Boulder, and Boulder Valley School District ballot measures remain to be determined. Staff also provided information on state ballot measures and said a legislative update would come in June.

Topic12.Title: Adjournment
Topic12.Summary: A council member requested a future agenda item to take positions on several ballot measures. The mayor then closed the study session at 9:23 p.m.
